title: Ocean Currents and Tides: Rivers in the Sea

questions.question: The chief driver of surface ocean currents is:
questions.rationale: Prevailing winds drag the surface waters along, while Coriolis deflection, gravity, and density differences shape the resulting loops.

questions.question: The warm extension of the Gulf Stream that keeps north-west Europe ice-free in winter is the:
questions.rationale: The North Atlantic Drift carries warm Gulf Stream water to the Norwegian coast, keeping ports ice-free at high latitudes.

questions.question: Which cold current flows along the coast of south-west Africa?
questions.rationale: The cold Benguela current chills the air over the Namib Desert; the warm Agulhas current is its neighbour in the Indian Ocean.

questions.question: The Kuroshio and Oyashio currents meet off:
questions.rationale: The warm Kuroshio and cold Oyashio meet off Japan, stirring nutrients that make these waters great fishing grounds.

questions.question: During El Niño, the first and most famous casualty is:
questions.rationale: El Niño weakens the Peru (Humboldt) current and its upwelling, so the anchoveta fishery collapses while Peru floods and Australia dries out.

questions.question: La Niña, the opposite phase of ENSO, typically:
options: Cools the eastern Pacific and strengthens the trades
questions.rationale: La Niña reinforces the trade winds and the cold eastern Pacific, often invigorating the Indian monsoon.

questions.question: The dominant tide-generating body is the Moon; the Sun contributes about:
questions.rationale: The Moon dominates tide generation, with the Sun adding roughly 46% of the lunar pull.

questions.question: Spring tides — the highest of the month — occur when:
options: The Moon is in its quarter phases
Sun, Moon, and Earth are aligned at new or full moon
questions.rationale: Alignment of Sun and Moon at new and full moon combines their pulls; at quadrature (quarter moons) the weaker neap tides occur.

questions.question: A tide pattern with two high waters and two low waters each day is called:
questions.rationale: Semi-diurnal tides — two highs and two lows a day — are the most common pattern, including along most of the Indian coast.

questions.question: India's best tidal-energy prospects lie in the:
options: Gulf of Kutch and Gulf of Khambhat
questions.rationale: The fast, high tidal ranges of the Gulfs of Kutch and Khambhat make them India's leading tidal-energy sites.
